status2026.detail: The APS directory entry retrieved on 9 October 2026 lists 19-ID-E as 'Operational/Accepting General Users', with access through on-site staff. Endstation and mirror commissioning began in summer 2025. The APS progress graphic assigned technical commissioning, stage 4, on 24 November 2025 and scientific commissioning and early experiments, stage 5, on 26 January 2026. The August 2025 update forecast first experiments for late 2025 or early 2026 and general-user access for the first or second 2026 run. An Argonne job posting on 31 July 2026 still listed 'commissioning and operation of the ISN' among the duties. User operations therefore overlap continuing commissioning. The spot-size target is 20 nm at 25 keV; late-2025 and 2026 abstracts report about 25 to 30 nm. The APS Upgrade project was formally completed in early 2026. Argonne's September 2026 nanoscience feature discusses ISN as a new in situ instrument.

tagline: A 220-metre X-ray microscope for measurements of batteries, catalysts and solar cells during operation.
summary: At the In Situ Nanoprobe, ISN, researchers measure materials during charging, heating or chemical reactions. X-rays are focused into a spot with a design width of 20 nanometres. This is about 4,500 times thinner than a hair; early measurements report 25 to 30 nm. The sample is scanned through the spot. At each point, elemental fluorescence, atomic structure, electrical current and optical emission are measured. Coherent diffraction patterns are used to reconstruct finer images. Heaters and gas or liquid cells require 5 to 6 cm between the focusing optics and sample. Long mirrors and coherent illumination are needed for a small spot at that working distance. The beamline extends about 220 m to a vibration-isolated concrete enclosure outside the ring building. Air temperature there is held within ±0.05 °C over an hour.

whatAPSUEnables.text: The smallest focal spot requires coherent X-rays, whose waves have a consistent phase relationship across the beam. Two small slits select this light and form secondary sources for the focusing mirrors. Before the upgrade, the electron beam had a horizontal root-mean-square width of about 275 µm and a small coherent fraction. In the design brightness mode, the width is about 15 µm. Emittance, the product of beam size and angular spread, falls roughly 70-fold. With the increased coherent flux, a 220 m optical layout gives a focus 61 mm beyond the mirror ends. The slits reduce sensitivity to upstream beam motion. At 20 to 30 keV, X-rays penetrate cell windows, water and gas. The 2017 design estimated focused-flux gains of 1,000 to 10,000 over pre-upgrade nanoprobes for spectroscopy, and 10,000 to 100,000 for wide-band mapping. The latter requires a multilayer monochromator whose installation is unconfirmed. Measured focused flux remains unpublished.
quantitative: The quoted electron-beam widths change from about 275 µm horizontally and 10 µm vertically before the upgrade to about 15 × 4 µm in brightness mode. Brightness increases by up to 500 times.

The final design, section 4-7.1, gives about a twentyfold reduction in horizontal source size. Grating interferometry at 3-ID-B has measured horizontal emittance below 30 pm·rad. The reduction from the pre-upgrade ring is about seventyfold.
Final-design Table 4.51 gives coherent flux after the beam-defining apertures of 7.2 × 10¹² photons/s at 10 keV, a 5.58% coherent fraction, and 4.7 × 10¹¹ photons/s at 25 keV, a 0.94% fraction.

At 25 keV, final-design Table 4.52 predicts 3.4 × 10¹¹ coherent photons/s in a 16 × 16 nm spot, or 3.1 × 10¹² photons/s in 24 × 30 nm with open beam-defining apertures. Spot widths are full widths at half maximum.
At 10 keV, the same table predicts 3.5 × 10¹² coherent photons/s in 39 × 39 nm, or 8.9 × 10¹² photons/s in 43 × 52 nm.

The MEDSI'25 JACoW abstract quotes focused flux above 3 × 10¹¹ photons/s at 25 keV. This is a design value, consistent with the final-design coherent flux of 3.4 × 10¹¹ photons/s. The paper reports no measured flux.

The 2017 design estimated a focused-flux gain of 10³ to 10⁴ for spectroscopy at 0.01% bandwidth and 10⁴ to 10⁵ for elemental mapping and ptychography at 1% bandwidth. The wider band requires the multilayer monochromator.

The design estimates Kirkpatrick-Baez focusing efficiency about ten times that of diffractive optics at 10 keV and a hundred times at 30 keV. For measurements without chemical-state contrast, multilayer monochromation with the energy-independent mirror focus gives about 25 times the crystal-monochromator flux.
The expected acquisition-time reduction is a factor of 100 or more.

techniques.name: Scanning X-ray fluorescence microscopy and fluorescence tomography
techniques.text: Absorption of an X-ray removes an inner electron from an atom. When another electron fills the vacancy, characteristic fluorescence is emitted. Its energy identifies the element. Scanning the sample through the focus gives an elemental map, including trace concentrations. Repeating at different sample angles gives fluorescence tomography. A seven-element silicon drift detector or a twelve-element backscatter detector records fluorescence. Fly scans reach 1 mm/s over a 10 × 10 mm area. Mirror focusing is independent of energy, so the planned 1% multilayer band would increase mapping flux. Ptychographic reconstruction of the illumination is used to improve elemental maps to about 10 nm.

techniques.name: X-ray fluorescence nanospectroscopy
techniques.text: X-ray absorption near-edge structure, XANES, distinguishes chemical states such as metallic and oxidized iron. The X-ray energy is stepped across an absorption edge, where inner-electron excitation becomes possible, and fluorescence is recorded. A spot tens of nanometres wide separates the chemistry of neighbouring particles. A liquid-nitrogen-cooled Si(111) monochromator selects energy to 1.4 parts in 10,000. Mirror focusing is independent of energy, so the focus remains at the same point as the undulator gap and crystal angle change. The 4.8 to 30 keV range includes innermost-shell K edges from titanium at 4.97 keV to tin at 29.20 keV. It also includes L₃ edges of rare earths and heavy elements such as lead and bismuth.

techniques.name: Ptychography and coherent diffraction tomography
techniques.text: A downstream detector records diffraction at overlapping scan positions. Computation reconstructs an image from these patterns at a resolution finer than the spot. The design goal is below 10 nm for sufficiently transmitting samples. The diffraction-limited focus is coherent, so ptychography and fluorescence mapping are compatible. The detector table has 6 m of travel and is also used for small-angle scattering and absorption. Planned data rates are about 5 GB/s, within roughly 10 PB of annual raw ISN data. Processing is planned on Argonne's Aurora supercomputer. Reconstruction also determines the illumination shape for checking mirror performance.

techniques.name: Nano-diffraction / X-ray diffraction microscopy
techniques.text: Crystal planes diffract X-rays at angles set by their spacing. A robot arm positions a detector around the sample to record these reflections. Measurements determine the crystal phase at each scan point and its changes during heating or charging. A 0.5 mm beryllium dome transmits a cone of about 0.25 steradian. Its axis is 10° upward and 25° outboard, away from the ring. At ISN, diffraction complements fluorescence during in situ phase-change measurements.

techniques.name: X-ray beam induced current / voltage
techniques.text: X-ray absorption creates charge carriers in solar cells and light-emitting diodes. The current or voltage measured at each scan position depends on local charge collection. These methods are X-ray beam-induced current, XBIC, and voltage, XBIV. Defective and effective charge-collection regions are compared with composition. A four-channel picoammeter records the electrical signal alongside fluorescence at each pixel.

techniques.name: X-ray excited optical luminescence microscopy
techniques.text: Some materials emit visible or infrared light after X-ray absorption. This is X-ray excited optical luminescence, XEOL. A vacuum microscope just upstream of the sample collects emission through a folded optical path with a central X-ray opening. Optical emission from perovskites or light-emitting-diode materials is compared with chemistry at the same scan point. The microscope field is 600 µm with 1 µm resolution. Light from 430 to 1,800 nm is transmitted to a fibre-coupled spectrometer. An external module supplies excitation or bias light.

scienceCases.title: Solar-cell film formation
scienceCases.text: Copper indium gallium selenide, CIGS, solar-cell films form at about 600 °C in selenium- or sulfur-bearing gas. Defects formed during growth reduce efficiency. Elemental fluorescence, beam-induced current and optical emission are measured at the same points to relate composition to electrical performance. A pre-upgrade demonstration required about seven minutes for each 10 × 10 µm map at 600 °C. The ISN design targets map times more than a hundred times shorter and doses compatible with radiation-sensitive halide perovskites.

scienceCases.title: Individual battery crystallites
scienceCases.text: Battery electrodes contain crystallites that take up lithium at different rates and may crack or degrade. Crystallites in olivine cathodes such as lithium manganese iron phosphate, LMFP, are only 25 to 200 nm across. X-ray absorption near-edge mapping with a 20 nm beam, combined with diffraction, is intended to distinguish phases within a crystallite during battery cycling. The as-built electrochemical holder has two fluid inlets, heats above 100 °C and accepts bulk electrodes and a flow cell more than 200 µm thick. It rotates for tomography.

scienceCases.title: Catalysts under reaction conditions
scienceCases.text: Catalyst structure and chemistry can change after removal from a reactor. The ISN gas holder maintains reaction conditions up to 1,000 °C, with two pressure-controlled gas inlets and four electrical bias channels. Design studies include iron and nickel poisoning in fluid-catalytic-cracking particles, chemical state near grain boundaries in biased copper catalysts for CO₂ reduction, and buried interfaces in photo-electrochemical devices.

scienceCases.title: Impurities in semiconductor devices
scienceCases.text: Misplaced metal atoms can cause insulating layers to fail in transistors only a few nanometres wide. Hard X-rays penetrate intact chips for elemental measurements within stacked 3D devices. Examples include high-permittivity insulating layers and copper or cobalt wiring at the 7 nm technology node and beyond. The 2017 science case described ISN as the only non-destructive method sensitive to impurity concentrations of 0.1% or below within small regions of an intact system.

scienceCases.title: Electrochemical interfaces for fuel cells and electrolyzers
scienceCases.text: Fuel cells and water electrolyzers contain thin precious-metal layers whose structure changes during operation. The 2023 joint ISN and PtychoProbe workshop proposed mapping electrode phases during manufacture and operation. Other proposals address partial gold and platinum films on iridium over 10 to 100 nm in liquid, where surface diffusion is faster than in gas, and vacancies in atomically thin hydrogen-evolution catalysts. The gold and platinum study requires a purpose-built electrochemical cell. The long optical working distance provides space for it. These are research proposals with no reported ISN results yet.

scienceCases.title: Environmental and quantum materials
scienceCases.text: Elemental measurements are proposed for valuable metals and toxic elements in coal ash, microbes at soil-gas interfaces, and underground carbon storage. For quantum materials, an APS-built holder with a closed-cycle helium cryostat spans 40 K, or −233 °C, to 355 K. It is designed for very low vibration and was still under development when last described. Workshop proposals also include in situ epitaxial complex-oxide growth and quantum materials driven out of equilibrium.

keyParameters.label: Photon energy range
keyParameters.value: 4.8 to 30 keV
keyParameters.note: The directory and MEDSI'25 paper give this range. The paper's JACoW abstract rounds the lower end to 5 keV, for 5 to 30 keV.

keyParameters.label: Focal spot, design
keyParameters.value: 20 nm × 20 nm FWHM at 25 keV
keyParameters.note: The directory lists 0.02 × 0.02 µm. Conference abstracts in 2025 and 2026 quote about 25 to 30 nm at 25 keV. Commissioning optimization continues.

keyParameters.label: Diffraction-limited spot vs energy, design
keyParameters.value: coherent: 16 × 16 nm, 25 keV, 39 × 39 nm, 10 keV; full beam: 24 × 30 nm, 25 keV, 43 × 52 nm, 10 keV

keyParameters.label: Focused flux, design / abstract value
keyParameters.value: >3 × 10¹¹ ph/s at 25 keV
keyParameters.note: The MEDSI'25 JACoW abstract quotes a design value. Final-design coherent and total fluxes at 25 keV are 3.4 × 10¹¹ and 3.1 × 10¹² photons/s. At 10 keV they are 3.5 × 10¹² and 8.9 × 10¹².

keyParameters.label: Optical working distance, end of KBH to focus
keyParameters.value: 61 mm
keyParameters.note: MEDSI'20 and MEDSI'25 give 61 mm optical distance. Final-design section 4-7.7.5 gives 60 mm nominal and 55 mm including the mirror enclosure. Section 4-7.2 and the preliminary design give 55 mm; SPIE 2021 gives 60 mm. Usable sample space is 47 mm in vacuum or 55 mm with the chamber top removed. The directory gives 20 to 50 mm depending on configuration.

keyParameters.label: Source-to-sample distance
keyParameters.note: The directory, MEDSI'25 and SPIE 2021 give 220 m, replacing MEDSI'20's 210 m. Argonne's July 2020 release used the exact phrase "250-meter (820-foot)", repeated by a contractor. The mirror geometry sums to 55 + 165.004 + 0.396 = 220.4 m. With a 220.0 m focus, the same distances imply a vertical aperture at 54.6 m.

keyParameters.label: Total beamline length, to beamstop
keyParameters.note: Beamstop 19ID-BS-1 at 227.0 m. The shielding paper also says the beamline 'extends 227 m from the source'.

keyParameters.label: Undulators
keyParameters.value: 2 in-line revolver undulators, APS21R25 #1 and #2, each switchable between a 2.1 cm, 112 periods and a 2.5 cm, 94 periods structure
keyParameters.note: Final-design Table 3.13 uses the exact configuration label "Dual Inline Rev 2.5/2.1 + Rev 2.5/2.1, phase shifter/corrector". Chapter 4 describes the pair as a revolver undulator of 4.6 m length with two periods.

keyParameters.label: Undulator K / first harmonic at device minimum gap, 8.5 mm
keyParameters.value: U21 first harmonics 8.35 keV upstream and 8.32 keV downstream at K = 1.38. U25 first harmonics 4.56 and 4.57 keV respectively at K = 2.00.
keyParameters.note: Values are calculated for zero emittance at 6.0 GeV and the 8.5 mm device minimum gap. User minimum gap is 8.7 mm; administrative minima are 8.67 and 8.64 mm.

keyParameters.label: Undulator power, per device, min gap, 200 mA
keyParameters.value: U21: 5.4 kW, 216 kW/mrad²; U25: 8.1 kW, 226 kW/mrad²
keyParameters.note: Final-design Table 4.48 gives 2.28 kW through the 2 × 2 mm exit mask for Kᵧ = 1.939.

keyParameters.label: Front end
keyParameters.value: HHL front end, 21 kW / 590 kW/mrad² limits, windowless, differential pumping, 2 × 2 mm² exit mask at 25.4 m
keyParameters.note: Power limits are from final-design Table 3.3. The 2020 shielding study assumed a 2 mm horizontal by 1 mm vertical exit opening.

keyParameters.label: Monochromator
keyParameters.value: LN₂-cooled horizontally deflecting Si(111) DCM, ΔE/E ≈ 1.4 × 10⁻⁴
keyParameters.note: A Mo/B₄C multilayer monochromator with 25 Å spacing and approximately 10⁻² bandwidth is also specified in the final design. Only the horizontal crystal monochromator appears in the directory. Multilayer installation is unconfirmed.

keyParameters.label: Beam-defining apertures, secondary source
keyParameters.value: BDA-V at 55 m, BDA-H at 64 m; minimum aperture ~3.5 to 4 µm
keyParameters.note: Using 0.44 λz/A at 25 keV gives coherence-matched openings about 3.6 µm vertically and 10.6 µm horizontally. The final-design fully coherent setting is 13.0 × 4.1 µm, horizontal by vertical; Fig. 4.50 quotes 6.5 µm vertical and 20 µm horizontal. Text gives a 3.5 µm vertical minimum, while Table 4.49 gives about 4 µm for both. For the flat-beam source, geometrical secondary-source full widths at half maximum are about 6.5 µm vertically with M2 at 29 m and 1:0.9 imaging, and 28 µm horizontally with M3 at 35 m and 1:0.83 imaging. The preliminary-design 16.4 to 18 µm horizontal width assumes M3 at 43 m and 1:0.49 imaging.

keyParameters.label: KB mirrors, as built
keyParameters.value: KBV L = 404 mm, q = 396 mm; KBH L = 129 mm, q = 125.5 mm; gap 4 mm; θ = 2.5 mrad; Si(100); figure error < 2.0 nm; roughness < 0.15 nm rms; JTEC
keyParameters.note: The final design places mirror centres 400 mm vertically and 125 mm horizontally before the sample. It specifies platinum-coated elliptical cylinders and numerical apertures 1.67 and 1.74 mrad at 25 keV. The as-built figure-error specification below 2.0 nm does not identify the metric, likely peak-to-valley. Final-design root-mean-square targets were 0.38 nm vertical and 0.45 nm horizontal.

keyParameters.label: KB angular stability
keyParameters.value: required 5 nrad, KBV / 16 nrad, KBH; measured 0.4 nrad rms, 1.7 nrad p-p, KBV, preliminary, in air with pumps off
keyParameters.note: Angular-stability requirements limit motion to 20% of spot width. Required relative spot-to-sample stability is 4 nm root-mean-square.

keyParameters.label: Sample scanning
keyParameters.value: 10 × 10 mm range, up to 2 kg, fly scans up to 1 mm/s
keyParameters.note: Vertical fly-scan speed is 1 mm/s for regions below 90 µm or 0.1 mm/s for regions below 10 mm.

keyParameters.label: Sample environments
keyParameters.value: vacuum, air or inert gas; 40 K to >1,000 °C; gas and liquid flow; electrical bias
keyParameters.note: The cryostat holder spans 40 to 355 K. The gas holder heats to 1,000 °C and the electrochemistry holder above 100 °C.

keyParameters.label: Endstation thermal stability
keyParameters.value: air ±0.05 °C per hour; instrument surface ±0.01 °C per hour
keyParameters.note: Passive thermal control includes an intermediate air environment, vestibule and laminar supply through fabric air socks.

keyParameters.label: Floor vibration criterion
keyParameters.value: VC-G vibration criterion, 0.78 µm/s rms over 1 to 100 Hz, on a 1 m thick isolated slab

keyParameters.label: Detectors
keyParameters.value: 7-element SDD, Hitachi or 12-element backscatter SDD, RaySpec with Xspress3 Mk2; 2× Eiger2 X 1M, robot-mounted XRD, 6 m-travel ptychography; TetrAMM electrometer; in-line optical microscope and spectrometer

insertionDevices.name: APS21R25#1, upstream revolver undulator
insertionDevices.type: Planar hybrid permanent-magnet revolver undulator with two structures on a rotating support
insertionDevices.notes: APS21#6 has a 2.1 cm period and 112 periods, with K = 1.38 and first harmonic 8.35 keV at an 8.5 mm gap. The alternative APS25#5 has a 2.5 cm period and 94 periods, K = 2.00 and first harmonic 4.56 keV. The estimated magnetic length, period multiplied by period count, is about 2.35 m, consistent with a nominal 2.4 m device. The minimum gap is 8.5 mm and maximum taper 5 mm. Rotation requires an open gap. The 25 mm structure covers the 4.8 keV low end continuously; the 21 mm structure gives higher brilliance at high energy.

insertionDevices.name: APS21R25#2, downstream revolver undulator
insertionDevices.notes: The selectable structures are APS21#7 with a 2.1 cm period and 112 periods, or APS25#2 with a 2.5 cm period and 94 periods. The listed 25 mm period is one of the two choices. Final-design Table 3.13 specifies a phase shifter and corrector between the in-line devices for phase alignment.

source.canting: No canting. The two devices share an axis, with a phase shifter and corrector specified between them in final-design Table 3.13.
source.frontEnd: The standard high-heat-load front end is based on the 28-ID design. Limits are 21 kW total power and 590 kW/mrad² peak density. Differential pumping provides a windowless exit. The sequence includes a clearing magnet, burn-through and fixed masks, photon shutter with intensity monitor IM1, GRID beam-position monitor XBPM1, safety shutters, and exit mask with XBPM2. The exit mask is 2 × 2 mm at 25.4 m; the following collimator is 5 × 5 mm at 26.1 m. Up to 2.28 kW passes the mask.
source.sourceSizeAndDivergence: Nominal zero-current electron-beam source widths are root-mean-square values. In flat-beam mode with coupling κ = 0.1, σx = 14.5 µm, σx' = 2.75 µrad, σy = 3.1 µm and σy' = 1.29 µrad. In round-beam mode, these are 12.3 µm, 2.34 µrad, 8.3 µm and 3.47 µrad. For a 4.7 m device at 25 keV, the computed single-electron photon contribution is about 1.7 µm and 2.3 µrad, from σr = √(2λL)/4π and σr' = √(λ/2L). Ring mode changes the vertical source size and required vertical-aperture setting.

branches.name: ISN nanoprobe line
branches.description: The two in-line revolvers supply a windowless front end. First optics in 19-ID-A include the mirrors and monochromators. The vertical and horizontal secondary-source apertures are in C at 55 m and D at 64 m, with the shutter in D. About 147 m of transport leads to 19-ID-E in the Long Beamline Building. The focusing geometry is fixed, with nominal sample position 220 m and beam stop 227 m. Final-design section 4-7.7.4 specifies fixed-exit monochromatic operation with Kirkpatrick-Baez focusing.

components.name: Upstream revolver undulator, APS21R25#1
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. two ~2.35 m devices, N × period and a short phase shifter share the ~4.8 m straight; centres drawn 1.25 m either side of the straight-section centre, source point = 0. Exact centres are not published.
components.text: This 2.35 m undulator contains alternating magnets that bend the path of 6 GeV electrons. Radiation from successive bends combines into a narrow beam. Two magnet structures share a rotating support; rotation is possible with the gap open. The 25 mm-period structure reaches a first harmonic of 4.56 keV. The 21 mm structure reaches 8.35 keV and gives higher brightness at high energy. At an 8.5 mm gap and 200 mA, power is 5.4 kW for the 21 mm structure or 8.1 kW for the 25 mm structure. The user gap is at least 8.7 mm.

components.name: Phase shifter / corrector
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. between the two in-line undulators at the straight-section centre, inferred from FDR Table 3.13.
components.text: A short magnet changes the electron path between the undulators. The resulting delay brings radiation from the two devices into phase for constructive interference. The delay changes with undulator gap. A phase shifter and corrector are specified in the design, but their as-built form is unpublished.

components.name: Downstream revolver undulator, APS21R25#2
components.distanceNote: Approximate, see the upstream device: centre ~1.25 m downstream of the straight-section centre.
components.text: This second revolver undulator shares the first device's design and axis. With their radiation in phase, the two approximately 2.35 m devices give roughly twice the brightness of one. Their combined magnetic length is about 4.7 m.

components.name: High-heat-load front end, HHLFE
components.distanceNote: Schematic placeholder: the front end runs inside the storage-ring tunnel from roughly 14 m to the FOE at ~24 to 26 m. No 19-ID-specific positions are published apart from the exit mask and collimator. The windowless exit uses a differential pumping section, placed at ~25.5 m in the 2017 PDR layout.
components.text: The front end connects the storage ring to the beamline inside the accelerator's concrete shielding. Masks absorb unwanted power, shutters stop the beam, and monitors measure beam position. Total power is limited to 21 kW and peak power density to 590 kW/mrad². Differential pumping separates the vacuums without an exit window, avoiding the associated disturbance of the coherent wavefront.

components.name: Front-end exit mask, with XBPM2
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This metal block has a 2 mm square opening for the central beam. Up to 2.28 kW passes through. A built-in monitor measures beam position. The 2020 shielding study instead assumed a 2 mm wide, 1 mm high opening. The as-built opening is unconfirmed.

components.name: Front-end exit collimator
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This heavy-metal block limits high-energy bremsstrahlung from interactions of stored electrons with residual gas. The X-ray beam passes through its 5 × 5 mm opening. The reduced upgrade opening confines the stray radiation for beamlines with small monochromator offsets.

components.name: White-beam slits, 19ID-SL-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49. A small pump stand, RGA, gauges sits at 27.3 m.
components.text: Four adjustable jaws limit the white beam, which contains the undulator's full X-ray spectrum. The opening determines mirror illumination and absorbed heat.

components.name: M1 flat high-heat-load mirror, 19ID-MR-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49, Knopp 2018 also gives 28 m. M1 and M2 share one vacuum vessel in the FOE drawing, NIMA 2020 Fig. 3a.
components.text: This water-cooled silicon mirror reflects downward at 2.5 mrad, about one-seventh of a degree. It is 400 mm long. Silicon, chromium and platinum stripes have different upper reflection energies; stripe selection rejects higher harmonics across 4.8 to 30 keV. The mirror absorbs up to 455 W. A cooled side notch reduces thermal bending about tenfold. The two-mirror arrangement lowers the beam by about 5 mm.

components.name: M2 bendable vertical focusing mirror, 19ID-MR-2
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This mirror reflects upward, returning the beam to horizontal. Its curvature focuses vertically at the slit 26 m downstream with nearly one-to-one source imaging. Bending also corrects thermal deformation in both mirrors. The reflected pink beam has a broad energy band but lower heat load, about 13 W here. The minimum radius is about 10 km in the 2019 design, compared with 4.38 km at 5 keV in the 2018 thermal study.

components.name: Secondary bremsstrahlung collimator, 19ID-SC-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49, listed at 29.7 m together with PM-1.
components.text: This lead block shields stray radiation on the straight-through path after the mirrors. The reflected X-ray beam follows a lower path. The white-beam stop is at the same position.

components.name: Photon mask / white-beam stop, 19ID-PM-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This block absorbs undeflected white beam. The mirror-reflected pink beam passes about 5 mm below it after higher energies have been rejected. The separation is estimated from 5 mrad reflection over 1.0 m between the mirrors.

components.name: Diagnostic flag, 19ID-BD-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This fluorescent screen moves into the beam for alignment. Visible emission at the X-ray position is recorded by a camera.

components.name: Pink-beam slits, 19ID-SL-2
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: These high-heat-load jaws limit the area and power of pink beam incident on the monochromators.

components.name: Double-crystal monochromator, LN₂-cooled H-DCM, 19ID-MN-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49, FOE drawing places it at ~31.4 m.
components.text: Two liquid-nitrogen-cooled silicon crystals select energy with a relative width of 1.4 × 10⁻⁴. Their angles change during absorption-edge scans for chemical-state measurements while the exit beam stays fixed. Horizontal reflection keeps added optical distortion out of the smaller, more coherent vertical source direction. Horizontally polarized incident light is reflected less efficiently in this geometry. The 2017 design estimates 83% reflectivity at 5 keV.

components.name: Double-multilayer monochromator, 19ID-MN-2
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49, FOE drawing places it at ~32.5 m. As-built status unconfirmed: the beamline directory lists only the H-DCM.
components.text: Two surfaces with 300 alternating molybdenum and boron-carbide layer pairs reflect a band about 1% wide. This is wider than the crystal monochromator's 0.014% band and gives roughly 25 times more flux for elemental mapping without chemical-state detail. The multilayer system is specified in the design. Only the crystal monochromator appears in the 2026 directory, so installation is unconfirmed.

specs.conservative alternative: d = 2.0 nm, 600 bilayers, 40% narrower band, 15% lower reflectance

components.name: Pink-beam missteering mask, 19ID-PM-2
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This safety mask absorbs pink beam if its direction changes beyond the intended path, protecting unshielded parts of the beamline.

components.name: Primary bremsstrahlung collimator, 19ID-BC-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This lead collimator confines high-energy bremsstrahlung from the accelerator to the first optics enclosure. It is the primary barrier on the straight-through radiation path toward downstream hutches.

components.name: Pink-beam slits, 19ID-SL-3
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: These jaws limit illumination of the horizontal focusing mirror M3. The opening determines transmitted flux at the horizontal aperture at 64 m.

components.name: M3 horizontal focusing mirror, 19ID-MR-3
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49; the NIMA 2020 FOE drawing shows M3 at the downstream end of 19-ID-A. NOTE: FDR Fig. 4.40, and the 2017 PDR label this mirror at 43 m, which is superseded.
components.text: This platinum-coated mirror reflects 5 mrad, about 0.3°, toward the ring. Its curvature focuses horizontally at the aperture 29 m downstream. The angled line ends about 0.9 m inboard of the source axis at 220 m. Either monochromator feeds the mirror. The 2017 design placed it at 43 m for approximately twofold demagnification. At the final-design position of 35 m, geometrical source imaging is approximately 0.83-fold.

components.name: Shielded transport 19-ID-A to 19-ID-C, 19ID-ST-1
components.distanceNote: Exact span 35.8 to 48.2 m, FDR Table 4.49; midpoint given. The FDR table says 'to 19-ID-B', but the FDR's own optics text places BDA-V 'in enclosure C' and the NIMA 2020 plan labels the hutch 19-ID-C, so 'B' looks like a table error.
components.text: A 12.4 m lead-shielded vacuum pipe extends across the open experiment floor from the first optics enclosure to 19-ID-C. Shielding permits use of the surrounding hall during beam operation.

components.name: Missteering mask and bremsstrahlung collimator/stop, 19ID-PM-3, 19ID-BC-2
components.distanceNote: Design position from PM-3 at 49.1 m, BC-2 at 49.5 m, FDR Table 4.49; one hotspot at 49.3 m.
components.text: A missteering mask and lead collimator and stop shield the entrance to the first aperture hutch. They absorb pink beam outside its intended path and stray accelerator radiation.

components.name: Vertical beam-defining aperture, BDA-V, 19ID-SL-4
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49; consistent with the NIMA 2020 plan, scaled.
components.text: The vertical slit is at the focus of M2 and closes to about 3.5 to 4 µm, roughly half a red blood cell's width. Light transmitted through it forms a secondary source for the final mirrors 165 m downstream. This reduces sensitivity to upstream beam motion and wavefront errors. An opening near 4 µm gives the design's fully coherent focus at 25 keV. Wider openings increase flux and spot size. The jaws intercept the beam at a grazing angle. With multilayer monochromation, up to 11.6 W is incident; head-on interception would heat a slit above 850 K.

components.name: Horizontal beam-defining aperture, BDA-H, 19ID-SL-5
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49; consistent with the NIMA 2020 plan, scaled.
components.text: The horizontal slit is at the focus of M3. Together the apertures define a small secondary source and reduce sensitivity to upstream optical motion. The design's fully coherent 16 nm focus at 25 keV uses openings 13.0 µm wide and 4.1 µm high. The horizontal mirror accepts a narrower beam than the vertical mirror, so its illumination remains coherent with a wider horizontal slit.

components.name: Photon shutter, 19ID-SH-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This water-cooled shutter blocks beam for access to the remote endstation while upstream optics remain in operation. Its pink-beam rating accounts for mirror-reflected beam transmitted when the monochromator is retracted.

components.name: Long shielded mono-beam transport, 19ID-ST-2
components.distanceNote: Exact span 65.5 to 213.0 m, FDR Table 4.49; midpoint given. Shielded ion-pump stations at 95, 124, 153 and 183 m.
components.enclosure: Experiment hall, LOM area and enclosed corridor to the Long Beamline Building
components.text: This approximately 147 m transport consists of 4-inch vacuum pipe, about 10 cm across, with lead shielding. It crosses the experiment hall, laboratory and office area, and an enclosed corridor to the Long Beamline Building. Shielded ion-pump stations are about 29 m apart. Modelled pressure is near 2 × 10⁻⁷ mbar at the pumps and 1 × 10⁻⁶ mbar between them. The pipe transmits mirror-only beam if the monochromator is retracted, so the endstation shielding includes this condition.

components.name: Double Si₃N₄ exit window, 19ID-WN-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: Two thin silicon-nitride windows separate beamline vacuum from the endstation. Window disturbance of the coherent wavefront is reduced by placing them at the end of the transport and omitting a front-end window.

components.name: Attenuator / filter box, 19ID-FL-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: Thin foils reduce incident flux for radiation-sensitive samples. They occupy the mostly low-vacuum beam-conditioning section on granite blocks.

components.name: Beam-conditioning section: scintillator BPMs, clean-up slits, PIN diodes
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. between the window, 213.0 m and the KB optics, ~219.6 m, on granite blocks, MEDSI'25 Fig. 3. No individual positions published.
components.text: The final beam-conditioning section contains two scintillator screens for position measurements, two silicon PIN photodiodes for flux measurements, and slits for blocking stray radiation. These devices are mounted on granite for stability.

components.name: Fast shutter, 19ID-FS-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49.
components.text: This fast shutter restricts illumination to measurement intervals, reducing radiation damage. It sits before the focusing mirrors in the endstation conditioning section.

components.name: Vertical nanofocusing KB mirror, KBV
components.distanceNote: Derived: q_v = 396 mm upstream of the 220.0 m focus, MEDSI'25 Fig. 5a; p = 165.004 m from BDA-V at 55 m.
components.text: Two curved Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors focus in perpendicular directions. The vertical mirror is 404 mm long, with a specified surface deviation below 2 nm from an ellipse. At 2.5 mrad, its projected acceptance is about 1 mm. The focus is 396 mm downstream and the secondary source 165 m upstream, giving about 400-fold demagnification. The angular-stability requirement for a 20 nm spot is 5 nrad. Preliminary commissioning measured 0.4 nrad root-mean-square angular variation in air with vacuum pumps off.

specs.stability: 5 nrad required; preliminary 0.4 nrad rms measurement in air with vacuum pumps off

components.name: Horizontal nanofocusing KB mirror, KBH
components.distanceNote: Derived: q_h = 125.5 mm upstream of the 220.0 m focus, MEDSI'25 Fig. 5a.
components.text: The 129 mm horizontal Kirkpatrick-Baez mirror focuses in the perpendicular direction. Its downstream end is 61 mm before the focus, leaving room for heaters and fluid cells. Chamber walls reduce usable space to about 47 to 55 mm. Maintaining this distance with a small focus requires long mirrors and the 220 m line. The angular-stability requirement is 16 nrad. Its shorter focal distance permits a larger angular variation than the vertical mirror's 5 nrad. Gantry mounting leaves space for the sample chamber below.

specs.usable space: 47 mm in vacuum, 55 mm with chamber top removed

components.name: Square pinhole, scatter guard after the KB mirrors
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. 'a square pinhole after the KB mirrors', MEDSI'25; exact position not published. Drawn ~5 mm past the downstream end of the KBH, 219.939 m, inside the UHV optics chamber, whose wall sits just upstream of the 47 mm in-vacuum sample space, MEDSI'20.
components.text: A square opening after the mirrors blocks unfocused light and light reflected by only one mirror. Fully focused beam passes through. The exact position is unpublished.

components.name: In-line vacuum optical microscope for alignment and luminescence
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. 'just upstream of the sample', MEDSI'25.
components.text: A vacuum light microscope shares the X-ray axis through a folded optical path with a central opening. The sample view spans 600 µm with 1 µm resolution. Visible and infrared sample emission from 430 to 1,800 nm is transmitted to a spectrometer.

components.name: Sample scanning stack and metrology, ISN instrument 19ID-BI-1
components.distanceNote: Exact nominal focus: FDR Table 4.49, MEDSI'25. Design geometry gives ~220.4 m.
components.text: The scanning stages translate the sample through the focus at up to 1 mm/s over a 10 mm range, with a payload up to 2 kg. Rotation is provided for tomography. Fifteen interferometer channels measure sample position relative to the mirrors through low-expansion Invar and Zerodur frames. Required relative stability is 4 nm root-mean-square. Diamond windows and a 2 mm helium gap separate the mirrors' ultra-high vacuum from the sample chamber, which operates in vacuum, air or inert gas.

specs.stages: Aerotech PRO225SL and ANT130L; APS vertical flexure stage

components.name: In situ sample environments
components.distanceNote: At the sample position.
components.text: Interchangeable holders maintain sample conditions during imaging. The electrochemical liquid-flow holder operates above 100 °C with bulk electrodes. The gas holder heats to 1,000 °C and has four bias channels. An APS-built cryostat holder, still under development, reaches 40 K, or −233 °C. Each rotates for tomography. The 2017 target was 10 K; the as-built cryostat holder starts at 40 K.

specs.media: vacuum, air, inert gas, flowing gas/liquid
specs.cryostat holder: 40 to 355 K, closed-cycle He, in development

components.name: Fluorescence detectors: 7-element SDD and 12-element backscatter SDD
components.distanceNote: At the sample through side or backscatter ports.
components.text: Silicon drift detectors measure fluorescence energies to identify sample elements at each scan point, including trace concentrations. A seven-element detector and a twelve-element backscatter detector are available, both with Xspress3 Mk2 readout.

components.name: XBIC/XBIV electrometer
components.distanceNote: At the sample, electrical feedthroughs.
components.text: A four-channel picoammeter is connected to the sample. X-ray-generated charge produces a current or voltage in solar cells and light-emitting diodes. Measurements at each scan position map local charge collection.

components.name: Diffraction detector on robot arm, Eiger2 X 1M
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. robot-positioned around and above the sample, MEDSI'25 Fig. 3; variable.
components.text: A robot arm positions the diffraction detector at different distances and angles around the sample. Crystal reflections are measured through a 0.5 mm beryllium dome oriented 10° upward and 25° outboard, away from the ring. The measurements distinguish phases formed during heating or charging.

components.name: Forward ptychography / SAXS detector on 6 m table, Eiger2 X 1M
components.distanceNote: Position is approximate. on a downstream XYZ table with 6 m travel along the beam, ≈220.5 to 226.5 m; midpoint shown.
components.text: The downstream detector records diffraction at overlapping scan positions for ptychographic reconstruction. The resolution target for transmitting samples is below 10 nm, finer than the beam size. A table provides 6 m of travel along the beam. Small-angle scattering and absorption are also measured here. Planning assumed about 3,000 frames/s on average and 5 GB/s of data.

components.name: Mono beamstop, 19ID-BS-1
components.distanceNote: Design position from FDR Table 4.49; drawn on the downstream wall of the concrete hutch, NIMA 2020 Fig. 3b.
components.text: This block absorbs the remaining monochromatic beam at the back wall of the concrete hutch, 227 m from the source.

instruments.name: ISN nanoprobe instrument, 19ID-BI-1
instruments.text: The granite microscope table rests on air pads during coarse alignment and locks when the air is released. Kirkpatrick-Baez mirrors sit on piezo-driven flexure stages in an ultra-high-vacuum chamber. The target focus is about 20 nm wide, roughly 6 cm beyond the last mirror, inside a separate sample chamber. This chamber operates in vacuum, gas or air while the optical vacuum is maintained. Diamond windows and a 2 mm helium gap separate the chambers. A shared Invar baseplate reduces thermal expansion. A fifteen-channel interferometer measures optics-to-sample motion. Fluorescence, diffraction, ptychography, beam-induced current and optical emission are measured in the same scan.
detectors: Dectris Eiger2 X 1M on Stäubli TX2-160L robot for diffraction and wide-angle scattering
Dectris Eiger2 X 1M on a 6 m-travel table for ptychography and small-angle scattering
CAEN ELS TetrAMM for X-ray-induced current and voltage
In-line vacuum microscope + fiber spectrometer, XEOL
sampleEnvironments: High vacuum, air or inert-gas backfill
Hummingbird electrochemical liquid-flow holder, >100 °C, bulk electrodes
Hummingbird gas/heating holder, to 1,000 °C, 4 bias channels

geometryNotes:
Two in-line revolver undulators share the 19-ID straight section. They have the same axis. The high-heat-load front end is windowless.

Inside 19-ID-A, mirror M1 at 28.0 m reflects downward by 5 mrad. M2 at 29.0 m reflects upward by 5 mrad. The outgoing beam is horizontal and about 5 mm lower, estimated from 5 mrad × 1.0 m. PM-1 at 29.7 m stops undeflected white beam.

The crystal monochromator at 31.7 m and planned multilayer monochromator at 32.7 m deflect horizontally inboard with a small fixed exit offset. The offset is unpublished. Mirror M3 at 35.0 m then deflects 5 mrad inboard. The downstream line has this angle relative to the source axis. At 220 m, the angular displacement is about 0.9 m inboard, estimated from 185 m × 5 mrad, before the monochromator offset.

The first optics enclosure, 19-ID-A, extends from about 23.9 to 35.8 m and widens downstream. A 12.4 m shielded pipe crosses open floor to 19-ID-C, from 48.2 to about 59 m, with the vertical aperture at 55 m. Adjacent 19-ID-D extends from about 59 to 66 m, with the horizontal aperture at 64 m and shutter at 65 m. All three are on the experiment-hall floor outboard of the ring tunnel.

A straight 4-inch pipe extends from 65.5 to 213 m. It crosses the laboratory and office area for sectors 21 and 22, then an enclosed corridor to the Long Beamline Building outside the ring building. The final design places shielded ion-pump stations at 95, 124, 153 and 183 m, about 29 m apart. The 2018 vacuum model adds smaller pumps at both ends of the 146 m pipe. The building exit position is unpublished. Final-design Figs. 4.1 and 4.48 are schematic.

The roughly 24,000-square-foot Long Beamline Building is numbered 444 in the final design and shared with HEXM at 20-ID. The same project built the adjacent Activated Materials Laboratory. Beams from the two adjacent sectors diverge by about 9°, from 360° divided by 40 sectors. ISN is the lower line on the final-design plan.

The 19-ID-E concrete hutch measures 14.6 × 6.6 m inside, with 12-inch walls and a roof about 2.8 m above the beam. A separate 1 m thick isolated slab supports it. The control area, airlock, sample-preparation area and wet laboratory are alongside. Along the beam are a window, filters, granite conditioning blocks, fast shutter, and ultra-high-vacuum mirror chamber on granite. The focus is 61 mm beyond the horizontal mirror end. A separate sample chamber follows. Its beryllium dome faces 10° upward and 25° outboard, toward a robot-mounted diffraction detector. Downstream are the green 6 m ptychography detector table and beam stop at the wall.

The vertical mirror reflects upward in the MEDSI'25 drawing, raising the focus about 2 mm. The final-design schematic depicts downward reflection. The horizontal mirror deflects by 5 mrad in an unpublished direction.

The enclosures from 24 to 66 m occupy about 42 m of floor. The following 147 m is beam transport.

interactiveIdeas.title: Aperture size, coherence and flux
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors adjust the vertical aperture at 55 m, horizontal aperture at 64 m and energy from 5 to 30 keV. The display shows secondary-source widths, transmitted fraction, coherence at the 1 mm mirror acceptance, focal width and flux. Estimated source images are about 6.5 µm tall and 28 µm wide at full width at half maximum for M3 at 35 m. The 2017 geometry with M3 at 43 m gave about 4 to 7 µm by 16 to 18 µm. Closing the apertures reduces focal width to the diffraction limit. Further closing reduces flux.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: The apertures select coherent illumination and reduce sensitivity to upstream optical motion. A smaller and brighter primary source increases the selected flux. Aperture width sets the balance between coherent flux and spot size.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use the coherence-matched opening Δ ≈ 0.44 λ z / A, where A = L·sinθ is projected mirror acceptance. Vertically, z ≈ 165 m and A ≈ 404 mm × 2.5 mrad ≈ 1.01 mm, giving Δ ≈ 3.6 µm at 25 keV and 8.9 µm at 10 keV. Horizontally, z ≈ 155.9 m and A ≈ 0.32 mm give 10.5 µm and 26 µm. The final-design minimum opening is about 3.5 to 4 µm. Demagnification is 417-fold vertically and 1242-fold horizontally; a 4 µm vertical slit and 13 µm horizontal slit each give about a 10 nm geometrical image. Add source-image width, diffraction width and figure-error blur in quadrature. Opening beyond the secondary-source beam width adds no flux. For flat-mode σx = 14.5 µm and σy = 3.1 µm, the vertical full width at half maximum is about 7.2 µm × 26/29 = 6.5 µm and horizontal about 34 µm × 29/35 = 28 µm. The preliminary-design mirror at 43 m gave 4.4 to 6.6 µm vertical and 16 to 18 µm horizontal. Round mode increases vertical width about 2.7-fold. At 25 keV the design comparison is 16 × 16 nm with 3.4 × 10¹¹ coherent photons/s, versus 24 × 30 nm with 3.1 × 10¹² photons/s with open apertures.

interactiveIdeas.title: Working distance and focal width
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors adjust mirror length, working distance from 5 to 100 mm and X-ray energy. The display shows focal width, numerical aperture and whether a sample cell fits. A second control changes source-to-mirror distance. Shorter distance requires a smaller secondary-source opening for coherent illumination of a long mirror, reducing transmitted flux.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Maintaining a small focus at a longer working distance requires a longer mirror. Coherent illumination of a wider mirror acceptance requires more distance from the secondary source. These requirements set the ISN length.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Diffraction-limited full width at half maximum is approximately 0.88 λ q/(L sinθ), with q = L/2 + W, following X. Shi, 2016. For horizontal length 129 mm, image distance 125.5 mm and angle 2.5 mrad, calculated widths are 17 nm at 25 keV, 42 nm at 10 keV and about 88 nm at 4.8 keV. Width is proportional to wavelength. Numerical aperture is half the outgoing angular spread, about 1.7 mrad. Coherent illumination requires Δ ≤ 0.44 λ z/(L sinθ). An opening of 3.6 µm at 25 keV and 1 mm acceptance requires about 165 m; 4 µm requires about 185 m. Platinum reflectivity limits the upper energy near 30 to 40 keV at 2.5 mrad. A critical-angle estimate is 84 mrad·keV/E, giving about 2.5 mrad near 34 keV. The final design fixes incidence at 2.5 mrad for the 30 keV upper range.

interactiveIdeas.title: Mirror-angle and temperature stability
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors change a mirror angle in 1 nrad steps and observe displacement of a 20 nm focus. A 'heater on' control changes a 50 mm steel support by 0.01 °C. Floor vibration is a second disturbance. The display compares these with low-expansion Invar and Zerodur frames, an isolated 1 m slab, laminar air supply and interferometric feedback.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Small angular and thermal changes produce nanometre displacement. Stable focusing requires control of mirror angle, support temperature and floor vibration.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Spot displacement is approximately 2·Δθ·q. For the vertical mirror, 2 × 5 nrad × 0.396 m ≈ 4 nm. For the horizontal mirror, 2 × 16 nrad × 0.1255 m ≈ 4 nm. These are 20% of a 20 nm spot and set the 5 and 16 nrad requirements. Preliminary vertical-mirror noise was 0.4 nrad root-mean-square and 1.7 nrad peak-to-peak in air with vacuum pumps off. Five nanoradians is an angle of 5 mm over 1,000 km. Steel expansion coefficient about 12 × 10⁻⁶/K gives 6 nm expansion for 50 mm and 0.01 K. Invar at about 10⁻⁶/K gives 0.5 nm. Air stability is ±0.05 °C/h, surface stability ±0.01 °C/h, and the VC-G criterion is 0.78 µm/s root-mean-square over 1 to 100 Hz.

interactiveIdeas.title: Measurements at the same scan position
interactiveIdeas.concept: A solar-cell cross-section is scanned. Selecting a pixel displays elemental fluorescence peaks for copper, indium, gallium and selenium, a crystal-diffraction pattern, a coherent diffraction pattern, X-ray-induced current and optical emission. Map views compare composition, strain and regions of reduced current.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Composition, crystal structure, electrical response and optical emission are compared at the same approximately 20 nm scan position.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Incident energy must exceed the selected absorption edge. K edges and Kα lines in keV are selenium 12.66 and 11.22, gallium 10.37 and 9.25, copper 8.98 and 8.05, and indium 27.94 and 24.2. Indium L lines are about 3.3 to 3.9 keV. An incident energy about 13 to 15 keV excites the CIGS K lines except indium K. At 30 keV, K edges extend to tin at 29.2 keV; heavier elements use L lines. At 1 mm/s, 20 nm pixels imply 50,000 pixels/s and 20 µs dwell. Ptychography requires at least about 60% overlap. A 20 to 30 nm spot therefore requires steps about 8 to 12 nm or smaller. A 3 kHz frame rate limits scan speed to about 25 to 35 µm/s. Ptychography also requires coherent illumination with restricted apertures.

interactiveIdeas.title: Transmission through an in situ cell
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors select window material and thickness, using silicon nitride, diamond or Kapton, with 0 to 2 mm of water and a gas path. An energy control changes incident transmission and escape of a selected fluorescence line. The display accounts separately for absorption of incident X-rays and lower-energy emitted fluorescence. At high incident energy, the available fluorescence lines depend on which shells are excited.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Both incident X-rays and emitted fluorescence must pass through cell material. Higher-energy X-rays penetrate liquids, gases and windows more readily. The working distance provides physical space for these environments.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Use Beer-Lambert transmission T = exp(−(μ/ρ)ρt). NIST XCOM water attenuation coefficients are about 41.9 cm²/g at 5 keV, 5.33 at 10 keV, 0.81 at 20 keV and 0.38 at 30 keV. A 1 mm water path transmits about 1.5%, 59%, 92% and 96% respectively. A 200 µm path transmits about 43% at 5 keV. Fluorescence escape depends on emission energy. For Fe Kα at 6.4 keV through 1 mm water, about 20 cm²/g gives 13% transmission. ISN uses single-crystal diamond windows and a 2 mm helium gap between chambers. The diffraction dome is 0.5 mm beryllium.

interactiveIdeas.title: Survey scans and local measurements
interactiveIdeas.concept: Visitors first map a 10 mm battery electrode or catalyst pellet coarsely, then select a particle for higher-resolution scans across three to four orders of magnitude. A clock compares scan time at ISN speeds with a pre-upgrade nanoprobe. One example locates a rare contaminant before a 20 nm-scale measurement.
interactiveIdeas.whatUserLearns: Fast scanning over 10 × 10 mm locates rare defects before detailed measurement. A 2 kg payload accommodates large sample cells.
interactiveIdeas.physicsToGetRight: Scan time is approximately row count multiplied by row length/speed, plus overhead. A 10 × 10 mm map with 1 µm pixels at 1 mm/s requires 10,000 rows of 10 s, about 28 h. A 10 × 10 µm map with 20 nm pixels requires 500 rows of 10 ms, or 5 s of motion. Counting statistics at about 10¹¹ to 10¹² photons/s and detector rate determine practical dwell. Maximum horizontal speed is 1 mm/s. Vertical speed is 1 mm/s only for scan regions below 90 µm, otherwise 0.1 mm/s. Planned annual raw data is about 10 PB.

funFacts: ISN is the longest beamline at the APS. Argonne describes it as sitting 720 feet from the storage ring. The instrument is 220 m from the undulator source and the beamstop is at 227 m.
The Long Beamline Building lines are about three times the length of typical APS beamlines.

An ISN concept existed in 2013 before the multi-bend-achromat upgrade. The 2015 Early Science design had a 180 m line. The final length increased to 220 m for coherent illumination of long mirrors at a 5 to 6 cm working distance. The 2017 design also places ISN and HEXM in one shared satellite building.
Preliminary commissioning measured vertical-mirror angular variation of 0.4 nrad root-mean-square in air with vacuum pumps off. This angle is equivalent to 0.4 mm over 1,000 km.
The endstation air is held to ±0.05 °C for an hour and the instrument surfaces to ±0.01 °C. Fabric 'air socks' blow gentle laminar air, and the exhaust fan is kept outside the room.
The isolated instrument slab is 1 m thick. Isolation joints separate it from the rest of the building. The vibration criterion, VC-G, is 0.78 µm/s root-mean-square.

With the multilayer monochromator, each beam-defining aperture may receive about 11.6 W, compared with 0.2 W using crystal monochromation. Head-on interception would heat a slit beyond 850 K and destroy it. The jaws instead intercept at a grazing angle.
The 404 mm vertical mirror is about twenty million times the 20 nm design focal width.
Planned raw data is about 10 PB/year. This is nearly fifteen times the roughly 730 TB combined output of pre-upgrade 2-ID-D ptychography, 2-ID-E fluorescence microscopy and the Bio-Nanoprobe.

Before ISN, the Structural Biology Center operated 19-ID for protein crystallography. It produced 2,277 publications. User support was planned until the April 2023 upgrade shutdown. The center has since concluded operations, with support transferred to the eBERlight program.

US Energy Secretary Jennifer Granholm opened the Long Beamline Building on 25 July 2022. Argonne held a ceremonial groundbreaking on 23 July 2020 with construction scheduled for autumn. The 2022 release instead dates construction groundbreaking to June 2020.

The 2013 and 2014 concepts proposed a 50 nm high-flux mirror focus and 20 nm focusing with zone plates or multilayer Laue lenses. The final upgraded-source design targets about 20 nm with mirrors and a long working distance.
Sample environments span 40 K, or −233 °C, to more than 1,000 °C. Measurements take place in vacuum, air or flowing gas, with stage scan speeds up to 1 mm/s.

openQuestions: The focal-width target is 20 × 20 nm at full width at half maximum at 25 keV. MRS Fall 2025 and XRM 2026 abstracts quote 25 to 30 nm. MEDSI'25 describes preliminary measurements as promising for the 20 nm target. A published measured profile and sample flux are still absent.

The final design specifies Mo/B₄C multilayer monochromator 19ID-MN-2, also depicted in the 2020 plan. The 2026 directory lists only a liquid-nitrogen-cooled horizontal crystal monochromator. Multilayer installation and commissioning are unconfirmed.

Published working distances describe different boundaries. MEDSI gives 61 mm optically. The final design gives 60 mm nominal and 55 mm including the mirror enclosure, with similar feature-page and 2025 to 2026 abstract values. MEDSI'20 gives 47 mm usable in vacuum. The directory gives 20 to 50 mm depending on configuration. Chambers and detectors reduce usable space below the roughly 55 to 61 mm optical distance.
Final-design Table 4.49 and the 2020 plan place M3 at 35.0 m in 19-ID-A. Final-design Fig. 4.40 repeats the preliminary-design position at 43 m. The exhibit uses 35 m.
The final design gives a 2 × 2 mm exit-mask opening. The 2020 shielding study assumes 2 mm horizontal by 1 mm vertical. As-built size is unconfirmed.

The final-design component table refers to transport from 19-ID-A to 19-ID-B. The 2020 shielding plan instead labels A, C, D and E. The preliminary design proposed reuse of Structural Biology Center A and B for first optics. Exhibit boundaries are scaled from the 2020 plan with about ±0.5 m uncertainty.

Most sources give 220 m instrument distance, compared with 210 m in MEDSI'20 and 250 m, or 820 ft, in the July 2020 groundbreaking release and contractor page. The exhibit uses 220 m. Mirror source distance 165.004 m and image distance 396 mm imply 220.4 m focus if the vertical aperture is exactly at 55.0 m. A 220.0 m focus instead implies aperture position 54.6 m.

Final-design Chapter 4 describes a 4.6 m revolver, while Chapter 3 and the 2026 device table identify two approximately 2.35 m in-line U21/U25 revolvers. An active phase shifter between them is not publicly confirmed.

The SPIE 2021 abstract quotes coherent flux above 4 × 10¹² photons/s at 5 keV and 6 × 10¹² at 30 keV. These differ from final-design Table 4.51, which gives 4.7 × 10¹¹ after the apertures at 25 keV. A transcription error is possible. The exhibit uses the final-design values.
MEDSI'25 depicts upward vertical-mirror reflection; final-design Fig. 4.50 depicts downward reflection. Horizontal-mirror deflection sense and monochromator lateral offsets are unpublished.
Flat and round ring modes have vertical electron widths of 3.1 and 8.3 µm root-mean-square. This changes aperture settings and coherent flux. Standard mode for 2026 user runs is unconfirmed here.
MEDSI'20 and MEDSI'25 specify 12-inch concrete walls, compared with 20 cm assumed in the 2020 shielding model. The exhibit uses the as-built 12-inch value.
The directory lists general-user operation in October 2026, while a July job posting still cites commissioning. Available techniques and sample environments are not documented publicly.

With M3 at 35 m, geometrical imaging at the 64 m horizontal aperture is about 0.83-fold, giving approximately 28 µm full width at half maximum in flat mode. The 2017 estimate of 16 to 18 µm used M3 at 43 m. The final-design radius near 11 km also corresponds to that older geometry. Measured aperture-plane widths are unpublished.
Argonne held a ceremonial groundbreaking on 23 July 2020 with construction scheduled for autumn. The 2022 release instead dates construction groundbreaking to June 2020.

The as-built mirror figure-error specification below 2.0 nm does not identify root-mean-square or peak-to-valley measurement. Final-design root-mean-square targets were 0.38 and 0.45 nm. The as-built paper does not restate the planned platinum coating.
